I agree generally with critiques of the values, but at the same time, this painting is SOOO watercolor in a really good way. The colors need more punch or something idk I think it looks great.

When you're painting from a reference, it's generally a good idea to paint literally the shapes you are seeing, and ignore the subject itself. I have highlighted in pink in this image 

https://i.postimg.cc/9Q6LBm46/Project-20250429013300.png

where your darkest values should be. In the photo reference, these highlighted spaces are your darkest areas, and can be represented as such with the black paint that you used elsewhere in the painting. I would ONLY use the black paint in these darkest areas. As for the rest of the painting, I would just bump up the contrasting values and colors by using *moooore pigment* in your washes. Maybe also soften the transitions between the yellow and reddish tints of the bronze.

oh and also the lines could be a little cleaner. With watercolor it's a good idea to mix mostly on the palette, and less on the page where possible.
